weaknesses.quote: From the second quarter on, the menus are the ones you have already seen in this run, so send the whole quarter in one reply: the Energy actions, the main action and `observe`.
weaknesses.problem: The Skill sends the main action blind. It assumes the choice numbers seen in quarter 1 will match the menu every later quarter, but no published rule says so. If the order changes, or an Energy action fails or is unavailable, the batched calls pick the wrong actions before the agent can see the menu. This also undercuts the later instruction to 'check them against the action names in the menu in view', because in a single batched reply the main-action menu is never in view.
weaknesses.fix: Keep one reply for the Energy actions plus `observe`. Send the main action in a second reply, picked by action name from the menu now shown. If you keep batching, add a fallback: if any `take_action` result names a different action than intended, or returns `success` false, re-`observe` and redo the remaining choices by name.

weaknesses.quote: N = 6 - (current_month mod 6), and N = 6 when current_month is a multiple of 6. ... In our runs it appeared among the events as month 6 (12, 18 … 48) began, before that month's stories, so it reflected the stats left by month 5
weaknesses.problem: The review deadline, the main near-limit trigger, depends on an observed timing that is unpublished and conflicts with the handbook. The handbook lists the review as step 9 after the quarter settles, so it reflects month 6 stats. The fallback ('keep the Review in 1 protection through that month as well') turns N into a two-month special case that a model can easily misapply. Calling month 6 'N = 6' while also treating it as possibly still pre-review is ambiguous.
weaknesses.fix: Define the review window directly: 'Months 5 and 6 of each half-year (5–6, 11–12, … 47–48) are review-protected months.' Apply step 4's strictest rule to both and drop the modular formula. Note in one line that the handbook places the review at the end of month 6.

weaknesses.quote: Level 4 or above: ... Energy: Skill learning (2) while Health is above 5, then one point on Prepare report materials ... Main action Apply for rotation.
weaknesses.problem: From L4 to month 47 this is a fixed loop with no Wealth or Dignity check. It also ignores that Skill learning costs Health every quarter. Health is only rescued once it reaches 5, which is late on a 0–10 scale that is also an ending dimension. The main action never varies with Network, even though Network is both a promotion factor and an ending dimension. The 48-month view ends at 'Skill first' and does not trade growth against the ending score (Health & dignity, Wealth, Network).
weaknesses.fix: Add a rotation rule for L4+: if Network is under its Best, or has not grown for two quarters, use Build a mentorship or Report results to your manager as the main action. If Health is 6 or below, swap Skill learning for Health recovery plus Prepare report materials. From month 40, shift weight toward Health, Dignity and Network so they finish high for the ending evaluation.

weaknesses.quote: From the second quarter on, the menus are the ones you have already seen in this run, so send the whole quarter in one reply: the Energy actions, the main action and `observe`.
weaknesses.problem: This assumes the menu numbering stays the same across quarters, and the published rules do not guarantee that. The agent sends all its choice numbers before it sees the menu, so the instruction to 'check them against the action names in the menu in view' cannot be followed. If the menu order changes, the agent spends Energy on the wrong actions without noticing, which hurts robustness.
weaknesses.fix: Batch the actions by name only if the interface accepts action names. Otherwise call `observe` once at the start of each quarter, build the batch from the menu shown, and if any result's action name differs from the one intended, re-plan the rest of the quarter.

weaknesses.quote: A mild risk (handling something privately, partially or later) is then acceptable when it is the only way to keep Skill, Network and Output, because a lost point there can cost the promotion.
weaknesses.problem: This review-month exception cuts against the Skill's own top priority ('no second hidden-risk blow-up'). It rests on an unpublished observation that one point decides promotion, while the handbook stresses sustained results and says hidden risks accumulate. The layered exceptions (strict mode, stalled start, review month, apply step 4 first) also make the step order hard for a flash-class model to follow reliably.
weaknesses.fix: Remove the exception, or limit it to the case where the HR remark has been friendly for at least two months and no risky option was chosen this half-year. Put the precedence order between steps 2 and 4 in a single line.

weaknesses.quote: `Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Reviews here: 0`
weaknesses.problem: Every story reply has to carry this bookkeeping: modular arithmetic, best-value tracking with resets, and review counting. With the long wording-cue lists and dense paragraphs, the document is heavy for a small model, and an error in the tracked Best values silently changes which option step 4 picks. This lowers clarity and makes the steps harder to execute.
weaknesses.fix: Shorten the note to `Review in N | Prev S N O | Reviews here: k` and compare Now with the previous note instead of a running Best. Move the wording-cue lists into a compact table, and cut the 'in our runs' explanations to one clause each.

weaknesses.quote: **Levels 2 and 3:** Energy: Prepare report materials, Network maintenance, Prepare report materials (start with Network maintenance when Network is under its Best). Main action Apply for a key project.
weaknesses.problem: The Energy plan for L1–L3 never spends on Skill. Skill is left to story choices, even though the published failure list includes 'skill falling materially behind organisational expectations' (Obsolete) and promotion depends on Skill. The fixed plan does not react to a falling Skill trend.
weaknesses.fix: Add a rule: if Skill is under its Best, or has not risen over the last two quarters, replace the two 1-cost actions with Skill learning (2) while Health is above 5. Make the main action Build a mentorship when Skill is the lagging stat.

weaknesses.quote: From the second quarter on, the menus are the ones you have already seen in this run, so send the whole quarter in one reply: the Energy actions, the main action and `observe`.
weaknesses.problem: Sending every quarterly choice blind relies on menu numbering staying the same. The Skill admits the menu may change but checks only 'the menu in view', which is the Energy menu and not the main-action menu that comes next. If the wording, order or availability changes, the agent spends Energy or picks a main action wrongly, and the rule fails when event or menu order changes.
weaknesses.fix: Batch only when the visible Energy menu matches the stored note exactly. Always send the main action in a second reply after the `observe` that shows its menu, or check the main action's name in the result and correct the next quarter if it differs.

weaknesses.quote: Every call resends the whole conversation, so the run stays within budget only if each decision costs one reply: tool calls in one reply run in order, and every result comes back before your next turn.
weaknesses.problem: The Skill is long and dense, and much of it is turn mechanics, token budget and note formatting rather than career strategy. The rules are nested and cross-referenced (step 2's review-month exception points to step 4, quarterly lines 1–6, a quick-reference table). This adds to the load on a small model and makes misapplication more likely. The note format also has to be updated by hand every turn.
weaknesses.fix: Move the turn-loop and status-line mechanics into a short separate block or a second Skill. Merge the duplicate near-limit material (step 3, quarterly line 2 and the quick-reference table) into one table. Cut the observation narratives (for example 'in our runs…') down to one-line rationales.

weaknesses.quote: Hidden risk** (not shown; the HR remark is your only gauge) is likely to rise with hiding, denying, blaming, shortcuts, gambles, fixing things privately or off the record, anonymous moves, side deals, partial, phased or postponed fixes
weaknesses.problem: A long keyword-cue taxonomy of option effects (Skill/Output/Network/Risk) is presented as heuristics, but it is a wording-based guess. Applied mechanically it makes the agent brittle when event wording changes. It also reads close to a rule set keyed to specific kinds of events.
weaknesses.fix: Replace the word lists with 3-4 principle-level heuristics. For example: prefer options that deliver your own work, involve others, and handle problems openly and completely. Tell the agent to trust the stat deltas shown after each choice over the cues.

weaknesses.quote: Every call resends the whole conversation, so the run stays within budget only if each decision costs one reply: tool calls in one reply run in order... **Quarterly phase: two replies in the first quarter of the run, one reply from the second on.**
weaknesses.problem: The mechanical turn-loop and note-format machinery (status line with Review in N, Best, Reviews here, and the one-reply pairing) takes up a large share of the document. It is partly built on assumed engine behaviour, such as the review talk appearing at the start of month 6. This is hard to follow and error-prone, and the document says so itself.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the loop to a short section: observe, decide, take_action, observe. Make the note one simple line of stats and the next review month. Drop Best and Reviews-here tracking, or move them to a short optional appendix.

weaknesses.quote: Pay rises with level, so an earlier promotion is also the main source of Wealth; ... In our runs Network and Skill usually filled up within a few months while Output lagged, so the quarterly Energy goes to Prepare report materials
weaknesses.problem: Level-specific quarterly plans are fixed from observation, such as Output lagging at the start and Skill gating L4+. They are not published rules, and they are fixed per level band rather than driven by the current stat gaps. This lowers rules_match and horizon quality. There is also no mid-game plan for Wealth, bonuses or end-state balance beyond month 48.
weaknesses.fix: Make quarterly allocation depend on which of Skill, Network and Output is lowest relative to its Best, with Health and Dignity floors. Add a short 48-month arc: early foundation, mid-game promotion cadence, and final-year balance of the ending dimensions (level, wealth, health and dignity, skill, risk, network).

weaknesses.quote: Network falls whenever someone is let down, even politely or fairly: turning a colleague down, setting a boundary, an honest but low rating, correcting or contradicting someone in front of others, naming who really did the work, reporting someone or going over a head...
weaknesses.problem: Presents hidden-effect assumptions from the author's own runs (and keyword-style cues such as 'Skill rises when you analyse...') as near-certain mechanics. These are not published and may not hold, and they push the agent toward cues that fail when event wording changes. Other lines are too specific to the author's observed runs, for example 'one point of Network or Output lost in the review month cost the first promotion' and 'a career still at the starting level at month 24 was dismissed'. The document is partly an event-pattern lookup table, which sits close to prohibited fixed answers.
weaknesses.fix: Keep only a short, clearly labelled heuristic: 'prefer options that visibly raise Skill, Network or Output, and avoid ones that sound like concealment, shortcuts or conflict'. Drop the run-specific anecdotes and the long list of exemplar behaviours, and tell the agent to trust the stat changes the game shows after each choice.

weaknesses.quote: Every call resends the whole conversation, so the run stays within budget only if each decision costs one reply... **Quarterly phase: two replies in the first quarter of the run, one reply from the second on.**
weaknesses.problem: The Skill is heavy on harness mechanics: the turn loop, the status-line format with Review in N / Now / Best / Reviews here, and the review-timing guesses. This is long, dense and hard to follow, with many nested conditions and 'first matching line wins' plus exceptions. A flash-class model will likely misapply or drop parts of it. The N formula, the Best-reset rules and the stalled-start rules are easy to get wrong, and the note forces bookkeeping every turn.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the Skill to about one third of its length. Keep a short turn loop (act then observe), a simple note such as 'month, level, S/N/O, Health, Dignity, HR tone', and a small decision table. Move the explanations of why into a few sentences.

weaknesses.quote: 4. **Level 4 or above:** Skill first, with Output topped up (in our runs these two held back most promotions from here)... 6. **Starting level:** every Energy point that lines 2 and 3 leave goes to Prepare report materials
weaknesses.problem: The 48-month plan is a thin table with a fixed Energy recipe per level band, based on guesses about which stat lags. It has no adaptive phasing for the economy (Wealth accumulation, the effect of promotion timing on salary), no mid-game check-in on balance across all six ending dimensions, and no link to the final score dimensions (level, wealth, skill, network, risk control). The endgame is one line for month 48 plus a story rule for months 46–48. The quarterly lines also say 'Showcase results'/'Report results' only in the endgame and never use several available actions.
weaknesses.fix: Add a compact phase plan tied to the ending dimensions: early build of Skill and Network, mid-game promotion push, and a final-year consolidation. Choose Energy by the lowest of Skill, Network and Output relative to their recent trend rather than by fixed level bands. State explicitly how to trade growth against Health and Dignity in each phase.

weaknesses.quote: In our runs it appeared among the events as month 6 (12, 18 … 48) began, before that month's stories, so it reflected the stats left by month 5 (11, 17 … 47). This Skill therefore protects Skill, Network and Output through months 5, 11, 17 … 47
weaknesses.problem: Relies on unverified empirical observations and an invented timing mechanic, and the document is long and heavily nested. The review-calendar logic, the 'Review in N' arithmetic, the Best/Now/Reviews-here bookkeeping and the many conditional exceptions are hard for a flash-size model to follow. The risk of confusion is high. Several rules are also self-contradictory: the quick-reference table says no quarterly phase falls in months 5, 11 … and gives a vague 'two months earlier'. The document also hardcodes 'month 48' as the last quarter while the handbook says events run to 48 with a quarter phase at the end.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the document to about a third of its length. Drop the Best/Reviews-here tracking and state one simple rule: in the 2 months before a review, avoid options that lower Skill, Network or Output. Keep one short, clearly labelled list of heuristics.

weaknesses.quote: Then also drop options that keep a problem private, anonymous, partial, phased or for later, or skip work to save time ... Hidden risk (not shown; the HR remark is your only gauge) is likely to rise with hiding, denying, blaming, shortcuts, gambles
weaknesses.problem: Asserts many invented effect mappings (what raises hidden risk, Output, Network) and quantitative margins (Health 5, Dignity 4, Health 3) as working assumptions. The text labels them as such, but they still drive hard-drop rules, and the 'HR remark' tone is assumed to exist. The wording-cue lists may mislead when event wording changes, and they come close to event-specific patterning.
weaknesses.fix: Reduce the cue lists to a few general principles. Say to prefer the option whose displayed result stats improved, and use the stat deltas shown after each choice to learn the mapping within the run. Make thresholds a soft guide, not a hard drop.

weaknesses.quote: Every call resends the whole conversation, so the run stays within budget only if each decision costs one reply ... Never send `take_action` alone, and never send `observe` in a reply of its own
weaknesses.problem: The turn-loop section is an operational token-efficiency protocol that mixes with strategy. It contains rigid, easy-to-violate formatting demands such as the note template, and the two-reply versus one-reply quarterly rule. This adds clutter to a strategy document and creates failure points if the tool schema differs. Also 'Main action Apply for rotation' and the fixed Energy recipes at each level are static, not adaptive to the stat that is actually lagging.
weaknesses.fix: Move the call-pattern advice into a brief 3-line section. Make the quarterly choice adaptive: pick the Energy action and main action that raise the lowest of Skill, Network and Output relative to the level, rather than fixed recipes per level band.

weaknesses.quote: From the second quarter on, the menus are the ones you have already seen in this run, so send the whole quarter in one reply: the Energy actions, the main action and `observe`.
weaknesses.problem: This assumes the Energy and main-action menus keep the same choice numbers in every quarter, but no rule says so. If the menu order or the available options change, the agent sends stale choice numbers blind, and it only reacts after a `success` false. That breaks the requirement that the guidance survive changes in order and wording. The opening line "choice 1 \"Continue\"" hardcodes a menu position in the same way.
weaknesses.fix: Tell the agent to choose actions by their label text, not by a remembered number. Allow the single-reply batch only when the menu shown by the `observe` that opened the quarter matches the recorded labels. Otherwise fall back to the two-reply flow. Replace "choice 1 'Continue'" with "the option labelled Continue".

weaknesses.quote: in our runs the half-year talk, the bonus and any promotion appeared among the events as months 6, 12, 18 … 48 began, judged on the stats held at that moment. This Skill therefore treats months 5, 11, 17 … 47 as review months
weaknesses.problem: The Skill builds the whole review-protection schedule around review timing it observed itself. That timing contradicts the published order, where the review comes after the quarterly settlement at months 6, 12 and so on. Several other mechanics are presented almost as rules: "the panel may show 0 while it is negative", "one point of Network or Output lost in the review month cost the first promotion", and "a career still at the starting level at month 24 was dismissed". Labelling them "in our runs" softens this, but the decision logic depends on them.
weaknesses.fix: Anchor the schedule to the published cadence: a review at the end of every sixth month, after the quarterly phase. Keep the observed timing only as a fallback that triggers when a review talk is actually seen in the events. Shorten the anecdotal claims to directional advice, for example "avoid losing Network or Output near a review", and do not give them as exact numbers.

weaknesses.quote: Main action Apply for rotation.
weaknesses.problem: From level 4 the stated priority is "Skill first, Output second", yet the fixed main action is Apply for rotation. Its published effect is Skill and Network, with no Output, while Apply for a key project gives Output, Skill and Network. The document is also very long, with nested exceptions such as the review-month exception, stalled start, strict mode, repair first and hidden costs. That makes it hard for a flash model to apply consistently and costs tokens on every resend.
weaknesses.fix: At L4 and above, use Apply for a key project as the default main action. Switch to Apply for rotation or Build a mentorship only when Output is at or above its Best and Skill is lagging. Collapse the story steps into one ordered checklist of at most 5 short bullets. Move the long cue lists into a compact table so the decision path fits on one screen.

weaknesses.quote: From the second quarter on, the menus are the ones you have already seen in this run, so send the whole quarter in one reply: the Energy actions, the main action and `observe`.
weaknesses.problem: This assumes the quarterly menu numbering and the phase flow never change. If the menu order, availability or Energy accounting changes, the agent sends a whole batch of wrong choices without looking. The success-false fallback only catches invalid calls. It does not catch valid but wrong ones.
weaknesses.fix: Make the agent match each action by its name in the last observed menu, not by a remembered number. Have it re-observe before the main action whenever the Energy menu differs from the one recorded in the previous quarter's note.

weaknesses.quote: This Skill therefore treats months 5, 11, 17 … 47 as review months (Review in 1) and protects Skill, Network and Output through them, and keeps protecting until the talk is in view
weaknesses.problem: The handbook places the review after the month-6 quarterly phase. The Skill moves the effective deadline to month 5 based on its own runs and then patches the gap with an extension rule. This creates timing logic that partly conflicts with the published order. The quick-reference row "(the quarter is already behind you)" is wrong at month 6 under the published sequence.
weaknesses.fix: Define the review window as months 5 and 6 by default, following the published order. Keep the observed early-talk timing only as a hedge. Correct the quick-reference row so the month-6 quarterly phase also protects Skill, Network and Output before the review.

weaknesses.quote: Every call resends the whole conversation, so the run stays within budget only if each decision costs one reply: tool calls in one reply run in order, and every result comes back before your next turn.
weaknesses.problem: The turn-loop section mixes harness and token mechanics with strategy and states assumptions about the platform as fact. It adds length and complexity: a 3-reply opening script, separate first-quarter rules and a fixed note format. A small model has to juggle all of this alongside a 5-step story procedure and a 6-line quarterly cascade. That hurts clarity and raises the chance of format errors.
weaknesses.fix: Shorten the turn loop to 3 or 4 imperative bullets: pair take_action with observe, plan the quarter after one observe, and add the note. Move the status-line arithmetic into one compact example. Cut the repeated rationales, such as the "in our runs" justifications that appear in several sections.

weaknesses.quote: From the second quarter on, the menus are the ones you have already seen in this run, so send the whole quarter in one reply: the Energy actions, the main action and `observe`.
weaknesses.problem: The batched quarter assumes the Energy and main-action menus keep the same numbering every time. If the order or wording changes, the agent sends stale choice numbers without looking. The fallback only applies after a `success` false, so a valid but wrong action goes through unnoticed.
weaknesses.fix: Tell the agent to pick each quarterly action by its name in the menu from the opening `observe`, not by a remembered number. Have it check the returned stat directions after the batch, and if an action differs from the plan, switch back to the two-reply mode for that quarter.

weaknesses.quote: Story: one reply with exactly two tool calls, `take_action` (the exact `choice` and the one-line note) and then `observe`, which returns the next situation together with the result of the action. Never send `take_action` alone, and never send `observe` in a reply of its own, from the Continue screen to the last month.
weaknesses.problem: Much of the Skill is token-budget mechanics, the status-line bookkeeping and repeated cross-references ("Quarterly line 6", "Story step 4", "Review in 1"). This makes a long, dense document that a flash-class model has to keep in view while it decides. The strategy is hard to find among the protocol details, and several rules are stated twice (the Health thresholds in step 3, Quarterly line 2 and the quick-reference table).
weaknesses.fix: Move the turn-loop and status-line protocol into a short, separate section or Skill. Keep a single set of near-limit thresholds and point the other places to it. Cut the hedged 'in our runs' explanations down to one clause each, which should shorten the file by about 30%.

weaknesses.quote: Quiet ("some risk, nothing serious yet"): first Energy action Defuse legacy risk, main action from the lines below. Anything else (frowning, uneasy, "you are on your own", angry)
weaknesses.problem: The risk response depends on classifying an unpublished HR remark against example phrases taken from observed runs. Together with the Review-calendar claim that reviews 'appeared among the events as months 6, 12, 18 … began', this ties key decisions to observed event wording and timing that the published rules do not guarantee. That cuts against robustness and the rules match, because the handbook puts the review after the quarterly phase.
weaknesses.fix: Define the risk tiers by the kind of signal rather than by quoted phrases: no warning, a mild caution, then an explicit warning or a red-line notice. Make Defuse legacy risk the default whenever any risk or trust signal has appeared in the last two quarters. Describe review protection as covering the months up to and including each multiple of 6, which is correct under either timing, rather than as an observed calendar.

weaknesses.quote: Before choosing, read every option for the likely sign of its effect on Skill, Network, Output, Health, Dignity, Wealth and hidden risk. The game does not publish these effects; the wording cues below are our working assumptions
weaknesses.problem: Large keyword-to-effect tables built from observed event wording (e.g. 'Network falls whenever someone is let down', 'naming who really did the work', 'in our runs a career still at the starting level at month 24 was dismissed') are invented mechanics and near-event-specific heuristics. They are presented with hedges but drive the decision steps, so the guidance is brittle when wording changes and risks being read as fixed answers for named event types.
weaknesses.fix: Replace the cue lists with a few general principles (prefer honest, documented, fully-resolved options; avoid hiding, blaming or shortcuts; trust the stat changes the game shows after each choice) and drop run-specific anecdotes and invented thresholds such as Health 5 or below.

weaknesses.quote: The handbook lists the review after the quarterly phase; in our runs the half-year talk, the bonus and any promotion appeared among the events as months 6, 12, 18 … 48 began ... This Skill therefore treats months 5, 11, 17 … 47 as review months
weaknesses.problem: It overrides the published review timing with an empirical guess and builds a complex calendar around it (Review in N, month 47 exception, 'keep protecting until the talk is in view'). It is convoluted and partly contradicts the handbook sequence, and the agent must compute it correctly every month.
weaknesses.fix: Follow the published schedule (review at the end of months 6, 12, 18 …). Define one simple rule: in the two months before a review, avoid options that lower Skill, Network or Output. Drop the month-47 special case.

weaknesses.quote: **Set the pattern in your first three replies and keep it:** reply 1 is `new_game`; reply 2 is `observe`; reply 3 answers the opening screen ... **Quarterly phase: two replies in the first quarter of the run, one reply from the second on.**
weaknesses.problem: The Skill is very long and dense, mixes token-efficiency mechanics with strategy, and the status-line bookkeeping (Review in N | Now | Best | Reviews here) plus nested exceptions in steps 2–5 are heavy for a flash-sized model to follow reliably. Some of the turn-loop rules (never send observe alone, quarterly menus assumed known) can break when the interface differs.
weaknesses.fix: Cut it to about half the length. Move the turn loop into a short checklist, keep the note to a simple 'month / stats / HR remark' line, and flatten the story decision procedure to 4 ordered rules without exceptions-within-exceptions.

weaknesses.quote: Stories are decided only by "Story decisions"; quarterly phases only by "Quarterly phases". ... In our runs the half-year talk, the bonus and any promotion appeared among the events as months 6, 12, 18 … 48 began
weaknesses.problem: The Skill is long, dense and heavily nested. Rules are hedged with many "in our runs" qualifiers, exceptions and cross-references (strict mode, review-month exception, stalled start, Review in 1/2). A flash-class model will find it hard to apply them consistently. Many of the "in our runs" claims (review timing, dismissal at month 24, the exact cost of one lost point) are presented as observed facts the agent cannot verify, and some conflict with the handbook's order of events.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the Skill to about half its length. Keep one short decision table for stories, one for quarters and one for limits. Drop the anecdotal "in our runs" evidence, or label it once as a heuristic, and remove the nested exceptions that overlap.

weaknesses.quote: Review in N | Now S.. N.. O.. | Best S.. N.. O.. | Reviews here: 0 | <short reason>
weaknesses.problem: The mandatory status line adds bookkeeping that the agent has to compute every turn (month modulo 6, Best-per-level tracking, Reviews here). This is error-prone and hurts token efficiency. The "Review in 1" logic also rests on an assumed review timing that the handbook does not state, so mistakes in it spread to the main story rule.
weaknesses.fix: Reduce the note to a short free-form line, such as current month, level and the weakest stat. Derive the review proximity from the month number alone, and drop the Best and Reviews-here counters.

weaknesses.quote: Missing a risky option costs far more than flagging a safe one: when in doubt, treat it as risky. ... a career still at the starting level at month 24 was dismissed.
weaknesses.problem: These are invented mechanics and wording-based keyword heuristics (for example "even through a formal channel" counts as risky, and the sign of each effect is inferred from phrasing). They are presented with great certainty and may steer choices wrongly when the event wording changes. The quarterly plan is also nearly fixed by level (always Prepare report materials plus Key project), which gives little adaptation across the 48 months, for example for wealth or the long-term balance of Skill and Network.
weaknesses.fix: Frame the keyword cues as weak priors, to be overridden by the stat changes the game shows. Remove the specific claims about dismissal timing. Add a mid-game and late-game plan that makes the quarterly mix depend on which of Skill, Network and Output is lagging, rather than on level alone.

weaknesses.quote: Hidden risk** (not shown; the HR remark is your only gauge) is likely to rise with hiding, denying, blaming, shortcuts, gambles, fixing things privately or off the record, anonymous moves, side deals, partial, phased or postponed fixes
weaknesses.problem: Long lists of keyword cues for option effects are presented as working assumptions, and they are a de facto keyword lookup that breaks when event wording changes. They also add invented mechanics such as 'Output falls when you coach someone', and the HR remark is described as the only gauge. This lowers robustness and rules_match, and it blurs the line between published rules and observation.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the cue lists to a short principle: choose options that are honest, complete and on your own deliverable; avoid hiding or shortcuts; trust the stat deltas the game shows. Keep any observation to one clearly marked sentence.

weaknesses.quote: In our runs Network and Skill fill up within a few months and Output is the one that lags: the quarterly Energy goes to Prepare report materials (Quarterly line 6).
weaknesses.problem: Empirical claims such as 'a career still at the starting level at month 24 was dismissed', 'one point lost in the review month cost the first promotion' and the assumption that reviews occur at the start of months 6, 12 … drive fixed per-level quarterly recipes. This is over-fitted and partly contradicts the handbook ordering, and the strategy is static: it does not adapt to the actual stat balance and it has no pacing plan across the 48 months.
weaknesses.fix: Replace the per-level recipes with a stat-driven rule: each quarter, find the lowest of Skill, Network and Output relative to its recent trend, and spend Energy on that one. Add a short pacing plan: build Skill and Network early, pursue promotion at every window, then bank Health and Dignity in the last year.

weaknesses.quote: Set the pattern in your first three replies and keep it:
weaknesses.problem: The Turn loop is very dense. It mixes tool-call mechanics, the note format, and the Review-in-N bookkeeping with Best and Reviews-here counters, and it has nested exceptions such as the review-month exception and the strict mode. A flash-class model will likely get these wrong, and the length costs clarity and tokens.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the note to one short line, for example 'month, stats, HR tone'. Drop the Best and Reviews-here counters. Reduce the story steps to four short priorities, and move the call-batching mechanics to a six-line section.
